subject.title: Feature: Distinguish webchat client types (Mac app vs browser)

question: Should agent-visible WebChat client type be exposed as gateway-attested connect metadata, as an explicitly untrusted diagnostic hint, or kept out of agent context?
rationale: Agents may use client type for native-only behavior, deep links, diagnostics, or privileged UX, so automation should not decide the trust semantics or carrier shape without maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Gateway-attested metadata
options.body: Propagate validated connect.client identity into a narrow runtime metadata field and document exactly what agents may treat as trusted.

options.title: Untrusted diagnostic hint
options.body: Expose only a clearly labeled untrusted hint for debugging and forbid capability or permission decisions from depending on it.

options.title: Keep gateway-only
options.body: Leave client identity limited to Gateway connection diagnostics until a stronger client-attestation design exists.

recommendation.title: Gateway-attested metadata
recommendation.body: Propagate validated connect.client identity into a narrow runtime metadata field and document exactly what agents may treat as trusted.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the Gateway protocol/runtime context boundary where steipete has the strongest feature-history signal.
